verdict.rationale: Devin's docs describe a hosted 'cloud Devin' that takes tasks through the web app, CLI /handoff, or API and runs sessions in its own workspace or machine, including macOS VMs, with multiple Devins running in parallel, so users don't run agent infrastructure themselves. missing for 10: an explicit first-party statement that all execution infrastructure is fully vendor-managed, documented concurrency/scaling limits, and independent hands-on corroboration of the managed cloud experience.

support.subject: As a developer, I can use a managed cloud offering to run agents without operating my own backend infrastructure

citations.quote: using /handoff to send longer tasks to cloud Devin
Delegating a more complex task via the web application and taking over in Devin’s IDE once it gives you a good first draft.
Run multiple Devins in parallel: Carve out independent tasks and run them simultaneously.
Devin can build and run Android applications directly on its own machine
Devin now has access to macOS virtual machines.
Configure it once, and every session boots into that known-good state.
